current.text: Smart joined the Rockets this offseason.
He is a bench player. The projected Houston starters are VanVleet, Thompson, Durant, Smith and Sengun.
The Houston guard rotation is crowded. Smart competes with Fred VanVleet, Amen Thompson, Reed Sheppard and Bogdan Bogdanovic for guard minutes.
Smart may lead the Houston bench in minutes. Ime Udoka coached him in Boston and values defense. Smart and Thompson could take most of the point guard minutes ahead of Reed Sheppard.
He could be a streamer or a stash when VanVleet sits.
Udoka plays his starters very heavy minutes, so bench roles like Smart's are capped.
With our March 28 end, Houston has a weak 3-3-4 fantasy playoff schedule, 10 games over weeks 19 to 21.
Houston has only 14 back-to-backs this season.
Houston is predicted to win 54 games and to play a conservative regular season without chasing seeding.

durable.text: He is not a traditional point guard, but he can bring the ball up and run the offense.
He takes good care of the ball and is still a really good defender.
His shooting is questionable. He is willing to shoot, but the shots often do not go in.
One expert calls him an assists and steals specialist who will not score much. The projections agree on the low scoring but show only about average assists and steals for the pool.

note: Smart is not a draft target for us. Yahoo ranks him 220 and ESPN 248, both value him at 0 USD, and our league drafts only 144 players. His line is low points and a weak FG% (about 39.6% on 7 to 8 shots) with only modest assists and steals, and Houston's 10-game playoff schedule hurts him further. Early in the season, check whether he leads the Houston bench in minutes, and watch for him on waivers as a streamer when VanVleet sits.
